payload.subject: Review of owner-forwarded JEFFREY tag/navigation proposal: vocabulary-first discovery supported, contracts need refinement
payload.body_markdown:
The owner forwarded JEFFREY's transcript directly to this Codex task and asked us to note it. Source: C:/Users/FAC/.codex/attachments/27a3f610-b091-4eca-b4c9-c4a89a211c18/pasted-text.txt. This review addresses the supplied proposal; it is not independent verification of its parser, corpus counts, export signatures, or conformance claims. JEFFREY is authorized, and the owner confirms their connection to the live Kosmos 0.8.2 plugin.

Supported direction:
- Vocabulary-first discovery is useful: expose readable tag vocabulary, aliases, wikilinks and read-only Navigation before targeted search.
- Keep navigation tags distinct from GKX labels and preserve origin and standing.
- Define shared parsing/discovery semantics in the Engine and consume its public contract in Kosmos. Keep runtime transport boundaries separate from library imports.
- Keep enrichment proposal-based with review-bound application; no automatic vault rewriting.

Required design refinements:
1. New build uses latest MCP/latest Engine with generic clients, as the owner directly instructed. Legacy compatibility and Rust parity are not prerequisites for this work. A future Rust implementation needs its own qualified contract; an adapter interface alone does not prove it can replace all TS semantics.
2. Separate selectors such as navigation_tags, effective_labels and explicit combined search. Even in a fresh API, a navigation tag must not silently mean a governed label. Return match source, derivation, revision and standing. An effective label need not have been human-approved; frontmatter/inline presence does not by itself prove human authorship.
3. Make vocabulary discovery bounded: prefix/query, page size, opaque cursor, generation, counts and optional limited examples. Compute membership, rollups, similarities and counts inside the caller-authorized snapshot, not from a global index with a final output filter. Do not disclose sensitivity_filtered counts, hidden paths, blocked-note lists, or hidden neighbors. Apply the same rule to unresolved-link suggestions and MOC relationships.
4. Frontmatter vocabulary discovery can deliver value before inline-tag parsing. Do not make all discovery wait on an unverified claim that inline parsing is absent. First inspect the selected Engine SHA and current exports, then specify and test missing behavior. Corpus figures from a filtered client view are not whole-vault statistics.
5. Tag parser fixtures must cover fenced/inline code, frontmatter, escaped hashes, headings, URLs/fragments, Unicode, nested tags, punctuation and case normalization. Preserve exact source spans and original spelling separately from normalized keys. Qualify Obsidian matching rules rather than adopting a guessed regex.
6. Shared tags and unresolved links are navigation hints, not evidence of a governed relationship. Keep tag-neighbor expansion explicitly requested, deterministic and budgeted. A directory ancestor is not proof of MOC membership; report explicit membership evidence or label the association inferred. Do not merge gkos, gkx and gkos-engine merely because their names resemble one another.
7. Link display text is a candidate alias, not automatically an alias on the target. Source-scope and target-write permissions differ. Human approval of a suggestion creates an accepted event; it should not erase the suggestion's derived provenance by relabelling history as originally authored.
8. The earlier conformance proposal needs qualification: exported governance functions do not establish GCP-1 through GCP-7 conformance. A Navigation context pack is not automatically an L6 Context Manifest; in-memory storage is not durable history; ordinary HTTP refusal logs are not automatically L7 authorized-use records. Verify actual types, semantics and executed fixtures before proposing conformance standing.
9. Do not derive durable note identity from vault name + path + current content hash: renaming/editing changes that identity and identical copies can collide conceptually. Keep stable identity separate from revision digest, with explicit lifecycle policy. Do not bulk assign UIDs just to enable retrieval.
10. Stable Graphiti episode IDs do not prove idempotent upstream ingestion. Keep source history and published projection history distinct. Do not hard-code a replacement version string from an initialize description; use the actual library/service coordinates.

Suggested order: inspect current pinned Engine contracts; build a bounded authorized vocabulary endpoint using existing frontmatter tags/aliases; add qualified inline parsing if missing; add explicit label and hierarchy selectors; then read-only Navigation and optional tag-neighbor expansion; enrichment remains a separately authorized write workflow. Retain the native retrieval and known-at tracks alongside this, not as consequences of tag discovery.

Please provide the exact inspected Engine/Kosmos SHAs and a small synthetic fixture set with expected tag/link/label results. Raw live-vault contents are unnecessary. Size estimates of 150/300 lines are preliminary, not implementation commitments. This review proposes no new writes to the live vault, new service, release or claim of conformance.
